🧠 Skills Framework

Human Soft Skills Map for PMMs

The human capabilities that become even more valuable when AI does more of the execution.

💡 The Core Insight

Humans guide and decide what matters. AI produces content. It's always a plus+ — not AI or human.

The skills in this map are not new. What's new is that working with AI amplifies their importance. As AI becomes better at generating information, humans get more value by framing, connecting, challenging, deciding, and governing the AI output.

How AI and Human Skills Collaborate

🤖 When AI increasingly...

  • Generates
  • Analyzes
  • Recommends
  • Optimizes
  • Answers
  • Provides information
  • Learns patterns
  • Assists thinking
  • Advises
  • Produces content
+

👤 Humans need to increasingly...

  • Synthesize
  • Judge
  • Decide
  • Think systemically
  • Ask better questions
  • Verify
  • Create meaning
  • Reflect on thinking
  • Take responsibility
  • Understand stakeholders

Thinking Core Cognitive Skills

Skill What it's about What AI does Why the human skill matters more
Stakeholder Management Address audiences correctly with right arguments, empathy Can tailor styles and simulate viewpoints, but doesn't know your specific stakeholders, relationships, or context Humans know what matters to stakeholders, can anticipate reactions, build trust, and customize output to be specific rather than generic
Systems Thinking Understand how things connect and influence each other Often optimizes one task but misses broader context and downstream effects Humans understand the whole system, anticipate downstream impacts, and avoid unintended consequences
Synthesis Combine ideas from many sources into something meaningful Creates many ideas but delivers fragments; information becomes abundant but siloed Humans combine different sources meaningfully — customer feedback, research, strategy, experience — into coherent decisions
Decision Making Steer AI direction. AI gives options, humans choose Generates options, recommendations, scenarios. But AI needs direction Humans decide which direction AI research should go, when enough info has been gathered, and which path to pursue
Judgement & Trade-offs Decide what's relevant, what matters, what creates value Can generate options but struggles when goals and priorities conflict Good judgement decides what matters. Humans evaluate trade-offs: speed vs. quality, cost vs. risk
Fact Checking Know what to verify and how to do it well Does excellent summaries but may misinterpret, hallucinate, or fabricate details Verification is a core human skill. Look through AI output, check sources, verify numbers and details
Critical Thinking Detect AI hallucinations, errors, biases, made-up interpretations Can be very convincing while being wrong — may lack context or introduce bias As AI becomes more convincing, humans must actively challenge conclusions, evaluate evidence, identify logical gaps
Embed Policies Know relevant company, state, and regulatory policies Can follow policies when instructed but doesn't know which apply to your situation Humans must ensure compliance — know EU AI labeling rules, company policies, and apply them correctly
AI Ethics, Bias, Privacy Ensure work is free from bias, follows ethics, respects privacy Learns patterns from data that may be biased; doesn't know what's in training data Handle input carefully, don't provide personal data, review outputs for bias, protect sensitive information
Metacognition ⭐ The crown jewel: think about your own thinking — assumptions, evidence needed to change your mind Can reinforce existing beliefs confidently — AI agreeing doesn't mean you're right Reflect on your own thinking: are you anchoring on AI's first answer? What evidence would change your mind? The more AI becomes a thinking partner, the more important self-awareness becomes

Collaborate with AI Practical AI Skills

Skill What it's about What AI does Why the human skill matters more
Speed Reading / Info Triage Identify important information in long texts, fast Generates and retrieves massive amounts of information in seconds Humans must quickly identify what's relevant, distinguish signal from noise, and set the right focus
Context Building Give AI the right background — enough, but not too much Uses context provided but assumes when info is missing — can lead to wrong outputs Determine relevant info for AI. Too little context = wrong assumptions. Too much = distraction from the task
Problem Framing AI solves problems beautifully — but humans define the right problem Generates output for the problem it's given. Cannot reflect on whether it's the right problem With AI, generating solutions is easier. Defining the right problem is now the critical skill — distinguish symptoms from root causes
Asking Good Questions Ask good, neutral questions to maximize AI output quality Output quality is heavily influenced by question quality — vague questions = off-target answers As AI makes answers abundant, value shifts to asking better questions. Break requests into objectives, constraints, risks
Editing & Refinement Refine prompts and AI results iteratively to enhance outcomes Generates based on feedback — first output is rarely final. Refinement improves quality Humans evaluate results, identify gaps, and improve both prompts and outputs. Structure, wording, logic all matter

Mindset Attitudes for AI Success

Skill What it's about What AI does Why the human skill matters more
Refinement Loops Build an iterative mindset: prompt → evaluate → adjust → repeat Incorporates feedback, adjusts outputs, iterates on responses Quality comes from multiple cycles. Learn from each iteration and continuously guide the conversation toward better results
AI Culture Support the team culture of how and when to use AI Makes work more efficient and can create value — if humans embrace it Foster positivity about new ways of working. Help others embrace change. Find your own balance to benefit from AI
Sustainability Awareness Think about the environmental impact of your AI usage Runs on data centers, energy, and infrastructure — even for simple tasks Not every task requires AI. Sustainability awareness helps balance value creation with responsible consumption
Communication about AI Be a positive representative of AI culture AI adoption creates excitement but also concerns, misconceptions, and resistance How you talk about AI influences colleagues' perception. Advocate for AI while understanding and communicating where human oversight remains essential
Human Creativity Keep your creativity! It sets you apart and improves AI collaboration Generates by combining patterns from existing data — can inspire but not truly create Humans use experiences, memories, emotions, intuition to create true new things. AI can inspire, but humans create meaning
Intellectual Humility Willingness to be incorrect — AI agreeing with you doesn't mean you're right Confidently provides answers and tends to agree with you (sycophancy) Humans must remain open to being wrong. Ask AI to challenge your assumptions. Be open for new views
Curiosity Willingness to experiment with and through AI Will support experiments and may surprise you with capabilities Curiosity drives us to try new things, discover AI capabilities, and grow more comfortable. Ask: "How could AI help with this?"
Cognitive Independence Find your human/AI balance Can act as advisor, collaborator, researcher, writer — performs many cognitive tasks Avoid outsourcing all thinking. Know when to rely on AI, when to think independently, and when human judgment should overrule AI
Patience Learning to collaborate with AI is a new skill that needs training Provides instant answers, which may suggest humans should already know how to use it Learning takes time. Persist through experimentation. Like any new skill, AI collaboration develops over time and through patience
